_note: THE FIRST NON-PLACEHOLDER ENEMIES. Landed 2026-08-25 from ENEMY-REVIEW.md after full review — every stat and effect there was ruled or explicitly inferred-and-flagged. These rows SUPERSEDE same-id placeholders from the hell-tcg port at assemble time; a placeholder never overwrites an authored row, and regenerating the placeholder file cannot touch this one. Effects use the closed vocabulary; anything the engine cannot fire yet carries `needs` naming a capability below, following the pattern the terrain badges set. Numbers are real but SOFT — sweeps own pricing. ROTTING FLESH RE-RULED 2026-09-05 (Angela): "In content, zombies have a 10% chance of inflicting rotting flesh. Let us change that to 2%." Applied to EVERY rotting-flesh carrier in this file, not just unit.zombie — attack.zombie.claw (which unit.zombie-burning, unit.strong-zombie and unit.fast-zombie all inherit by sameAs, so four units change), attack.zombie-hound.bite and move.zombie-hound.close-bite. NOT touched, because they are different afflictions and were not ruled on: werewolf lycanthropy 10, vampire vampirism 20, vampire-lord vampirism 30, ghost possession 25.

capabilities._note: Everything a row below needs that the engine does not have. All design-ruled in ENEMY-REVIEW.md 2026-08-23; none is an open question. A row naming one of these is complete content waiting on engine work, not a gap in the content.
capabilities.capability.power: The power pool. Integer; fractions resolve nearest, 0.5 up. Gained three ways (external pool / one-time on arrival / escalating clock or condition); consumers read it and mostly do not feed it.
capabilities.capability.inflict-affliction: Apply an affliction badge (possession | vampirism | lycanthropy | rotting-flesh — the family of exactly four) to a hero in combat. The badge swaps the hero's art to the affliction portrait already in art/heroes/<slug>/card/.
capabilities.capability.corpses: Corpse tokens as board objects. Created when any enemy is downed and when a hero actually dies (deathbed check → unconscious → bleed-out timer → corpse). Raising a corpse is summoning. One universal corpse art for heroes.
capabilities.capability.ground-layers: Poison and cursed as ground layers alongside burning and frost (same ask as Creeping Blight's 'blighted').
capabilities.capability.target-stamina-loss: The existing stamina loss, aimed at a target instead of paid as a cost. Same loss, normal recovery — one mechanism, new direction.
capabilities.capability.line-shape: A line area shape, plus 'furthest target in range' as a selector. Granted 2026-08-23.
capabilities.capability.enemy-action-cooldown: Cooldown/warmup on enemy actions — the fields hero powers already carry, reused.
capabilities.capability.giant-footprint: 3-hex footprint (one below, two above). No terrain movement costs; takes every affliction and trap on all tiles crossed. PARKED — not for a while.
capabilities.capability.stealth: A unit that cannot be targeted and does not appear on the map; moving onto its hex stops the move. Designed in COMBAT-DESIGN (Vision, darkness, fog and stealth) and never built. The Nightstalker re-enters it at End of Activation while standing on darkness, and rule.stealth-does-not-hold reveals one stealthed unit each Phase.

units.name: Ghost
units.source: Ruled 2026-09-29 (Andrew, engine/DECISIONS.md "the Ghost as the bestiary has it; Cold Resist; ..."): "Should the Ghost go in with its bestiary numbers as-is ...?" — "Yes." · "Ghost should inflict possession". Ported as-is from gen/bestiary.json unit.ghost (rank 1: Strength 4, Precision 5, Armor 0, Health 4, Reach 1, Resist 0, Dodge 10; derived Accuracy 85, Movement 5; types Ghost and Flying — Flying is the flight move). Possess: the bestiary rider (gen/bestiary-riders.json, 25%, SOFT), fired onHit because Possess deals 0 — Magic 0 + 0 is exactly the authored 0 (engine SWITCHES ghostPossessReadsMagic). Attack: the bestiary gives it no number; it reads Strength, magic-typed (engine SWITCHES ghostAttackReadsStrength). Phase ("grant a stat for the Battle", value 2, no stat named) is left out — the bestiary names no stat. Family oddballs: no ghost family exists.
